text: Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the LORD lives, the God of Israel in whose presence I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these coming years except at my word."
Then the word of the LORD came to him:
"Leave this place, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
You shall drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."
So he went and did as the LORD had said. He went and settled by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.
But after a while the wadi dried up, for there had been no rain in the land.
Then the word of the LORD came to him:
"Get up and go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. I have commanded a widow there to feed you."
So he got up and went to Zarephath. When he came to the entrance of the town, there was a widow gathering sticks. He called to her and said, "Please bring me a little water in a jar, so I may drink."
As she went to get it, he called after her and said, "Please bring me a piece of bread as well."

But she answered, "As the LORD your God lives, I have nothing baked—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a couple of sticks now, and I will go in and prepare it for myself and my son, and we will eat it and die."
Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go and do as you have said, but first make me a small loaf from what you have and bring it out to me. Then make something for yourself and your son,
for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not run dry, until the day the LORD sends rain on the face of the ground.'"

versions.text: for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not run dry, until the day the LORD sends rain on the face of the earth.'"
versions.explanation: אֲדָמָה refers to the soil or farmland rather than the earth as a whole; "the ground" better fits the drought context of the chapter.

text: She went and did as Elijah had said, and she and Elijah and her household ate for many days.

versions.text: She went and did as Elijah had said, and she and he and her household ate for many days.
versions.explanation: "She and he" is ambiguous and stumbles when read aloud; naming Elijah keeps the Hebrew word order (woman first) while making the referent clear for a listener.

text: The jar of flour did not run out, and the jug of oil did not run dry, just as the LORD had spoken through Elijah.
Some time later the son of the woman who owned the house fell ill. His illness grew so severe that there was no breath left in him.
She said to Elijah, "What have I to do with you, man of God? Have you come to me to bring my sin to mind and to kill my son?"
He said to her, "Give me your son." He took him from her arms, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
Then he cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, have you brought disaster even on the widow I am staying with, by killing her son?"

versions.text: Then he cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, have you brought disaster even on this widow who has taken me in, by killing her son?"
versions.explanation: מִתְגּוֹרֵר עִמָּהּ describes Elijah's own sojourning with her rather than her act of taking him in; the revision keeps the Hebrew focus and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: He stretched himself out over the boy three times and cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, let this boy's life return to him."
The LORD heard Elijah's voice, and the boy's life returned to him, and he lived.
Elijah took the boy, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. "Look," Elijah said, "your son is alive."
Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth."
